verses.1: And great misfortune befell Yonah. He was destroyed.
verses.2: And he prayed to the LORD, saying, “O LORD, I have spoken these words while I was still on my own land. Therefore, I dared to do this. I knew that you are the Almighty God, full of compassion and kindness. Your mercy is eternal, and you are always willing to comfort those who suffer.”
verses.3: And now, Lord, please take my soul away from me, for it is better for me to die than to continue living in this state.
verses.4: And Jehovah said, “You have been chosen for this task.”
verses.5: And Yona went out of the city. He settled down in a place outside the city, and he built a tent there. He stayed under that tent until he saw what would happen in the city.
verses.6: And Jehovah God created Kikion, and He placed him above Jonah, so that he could serve as a shadow over Jonah’s head, thereby protecting him from his enemies. Jonah was very happy with Kikion.
verses.7: And God made a hole in the black clouds at night. He cut through the clouds, and they became dry.
verses.8: And it happened that, as the sun rose, God sent a strong wind. The sun shone upon Yona’s head, and he was terrified. He asked for death to end his suffering. He said, “I prefer death over living.”
verses.9: And God said to Yonah, “Yonah, I have chosen you to carry the message of the covenant. And He said, “I have chosen you until my death.”
verses.10: And the LORD said, “You have shown kindness to those who did not work hard for it, and who were not raised up during the night. But they died during the night.”
verses.11: And I do not dwell in that great city, where there are more than twenty-one thousand people. They do not even know each other, nor do they know the animals that live there.
